newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto aides re-arrested after court freed them.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto aides re-arrested after court freed them.

text.p: Pakistani police on Thursday re-arrested two aides to ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto after a court ordered their release.

Bhutto's political secretary Naheed Khan and former science and technology minister Nawaz Khokhar were picked up by the Federal Investigation Agency shortly after the Punjab province's Lahore High Court ordered their release from detention, a spokesman for Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party said.
Khokhar was detained last week and Naheed on Tuesday on unspecified charges under a Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance.
Police confirmed the two had been re-arrested but declined to give reasons for the action.

It was the latest in a series of detentions after President Farooq Leghari dissolved the lower house of parliament and sacked Bhutto's three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Other people detained under the same ordinance include Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari.
Bhutto has challenged the detention of Zardari, who was also investment minister in her cabinet, before the Punjab province's Lahore High Court.
